questions.question: Why did LSTMs become a bottleneck for training very large language models?
options: They could not process any text at all
They had to read words sequentially, making training slow
They used too many output layers
They only worked on images

questions.question: What was the key idea behind the Transformer breakthrough in 2017?
options: Replace attention with more memory cells
Delete the slow word-by-word recurrence and process all words in parallel
Use only convolution for language
Train models without data

questions.question: The paper "Attention Is All You Need" introduced which architecture?
options: RNN
LSTM
Transformer
CNN

questions.question: In self-attention, what does the Query (Q) represent?
options: The actual meaning stored inside a word
What the model is looking for
The position of the word in a sentence
The final output token

questions.question: In the QKV system, what is the best description of a Key (K)?
options: A label used to describe what a word is about
The generated answer from the decoder
The exact order number of a word
The loss value of a token

questions.question: In the QKV system, the Value (V) most closely represents:
options: The hidden meaning or information associated with the word
The query sentence itself
The word's position only
The softmax score after normalization

questions.question: When the Transformer reads the sentence 'I sat by the river bank,' why does the word 'river' help interpret 'bank' correctly?
options: Because 'river' is always the first token
Because the Query for 'bank' strongly matches the Key of 'river'
Because the decoder ignores nearby words
Because the sentence has only one possible meaning

questions.question: What does the softmax function do in attention?
options: It converts raw scores into probabilities that sum to 100%
It deletes unimportant words permanently
It creates the word positions
It trains the model faster by itself

questions.question: The main role of the Encoder in a Transformer is to:
options: Generate the final answer token by token
Read the prompt and build a rich numerical representation of it
Forget earlier words quickly
Translate pixels into text

questions.question: The Decoder in a Transformer mainly:
options: Reads images and labels them
Predicts the output one token at a time
Stores all training data in memory
Removes positional information

questions.question: Why does the Decoder also use attention on the words it has already generated?
options: To repeat the same token many times
To maintain grammar and avoid losing track of context
To eliminate the need for training
To convert the input into images

questions.question: If a Transformer did not use positional encoding, what would be the biggest problem?
options: It would not be able to multiply matrices
It would not know the order of words in a sentence
It would stop using attention
It would only work on short prompts

questions.question: Positional Encoding can best be thought of as:
options: A memory chip inside the decoder
A mathematical time stamp added to each word
A loss function used in training
A type of activation function

questions.question: Why is the sentence 'The dog bit the man' different from 'The man bit the dog'?
options: Because the words are different lengths
Because word order changes meaning
Because both sentences have no subject
Because attention cannot read verbs

questions.question: What is the greatest advantage of Transformers over LSTMs mentioned in the chapter?
options: They process text sequentially with more memory
They can process all words at the same time using parallel processing
They remove the need for any mathematical operations
They only work on very small sentences

questions.question: The self-attention mechanism helps the model mainly by:
options: Focusing on important relationships between words
Replacing all tokens with images
Deleting the need for encoders
Making every word equally important

questions.question: In the library analogy, what does the Key most closely resemble?
options: The label on the outside of a file cabinet
The researcher's final report
The physical shelf number only
The reading speed of the student

questions.question: What happens when the Query for one word strongly matches the Key of another word?
options: The model ignores the other word
The model gives that related word higher attention
The model removes positional encoding
The model stops processing the sentence

questions.question: Why did Transformers enable the creation of massive LLMs more effectively than earlier sequence models?
options: They could ignore all input data
They could process long documents much faster while preserving relationships between words
They only required one training example
They never used attention

questions.question: Which option correctly matches the role in a Transformer?
options: Encoder = writes the answer; Decoder = reads the prompt
Encoder = builds context from input; Decoder = generates output tokens
Encoder = stores positions; Decoder = creates filters
Encoder = performs pooling; Decoder = performs convolution
